entities.summary: Jan Roháč of Dubá was a Bohemian Hussite general who originated in the Bohemian gentry. He led the Hussite uprising against the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire, employing innovative tactics and mobilizing a large force of peasant soldiers. This movement resulted in the establishment of the Hussite state, which existed from 1419 to 1436, and had a lasting impact on European politics and religion. The movement's emphasis on individual conscience and the authority of scripture also influenced the development of Protestantism. Jan Roháč of Dubá played a key role in shaping the movement, but his ultimate fate was sealed when he was killed in battle on September 18, 1437. This event marked the end of the Hussite uprising and the beginning of a new era in European history. The Hussite movement's legacy can be seen in the continued struggle for religious freedom and the importance of individual conscience in shaping political and social change.

entities.summary: Jan Roháč of Dubá was a Bohemian Hussite general who originated in the Bohemian gentry and played a key role in the Hussite Wars, a pivotal conflict in the history of the Holy Roman Empire. Born around 1400, Roháč was a prominent military leader who commanded the Hussite forces in several battles, including the Battle of Lipany in 1434. His military strategies and leadership skills were instrumental in the Hussite movement's success, which sought to reform the Catholic Church and promote the principles of the Hussite movement. Roháč's legacy as a military leader and his role in shaping the course of the Hussite Wars continue to be studied by historians today. The Hussite Wars, in which Roháč played a crucial role, had a profound impact on the history of the Holy Roman Empire, contributing to the decline of the empire's power and the rise of Protestantism in Europe. As a key figure in the movement, Roháč's actions and decisions helped to shape the future of Christianity in Europe and left a lasting legacy in the region.
